quote: Using the azoxymethane and dextran sodium sulfate colitis-associated colorectal cancer model, we show that caspase-1-deficient (Casp1(-/-)) mice have enhanced tumor formation.
summary: Caspase-1-deficient mice developed more tumours in the AOM/DSS colitis-associated cancer model, through effects on epithelial proliferation and apoptosis rather than inflammation.

quote: Analysis of Casp1-/-Casp8-/- mice revealed a functional Caspase-8 inflammasome in vivo.
summary: Caspase-1 acts with caspase-8 in epithelial inflammasome responses that protect against Salmonella but can cause pathology; the net direction for caspase-1 alone is unclear.

quote: We conclude that inhibition of ICE represents a novel anti-inflammatory strategy for intestinal inflammation.
summary: ICE (caspase-1) knockout mice were strongly protected from acute and chronic DSS colitis, with lower IL-18, IL-1 beta and IFN-gamma.

quote: The RNA sequencing analysis of renal cortex revealed that the nlrp3 or casp1 knockout CI-AKI mice exhibited upregulated cellular response to hypoxia, mitochondrial oxidation, and autophagy when compared with the wild-type (WT) CI-AKI mice, which indicated that NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition resulted in the upregulation of hypoxia signaling pathway and mitophagy.
summary: In a kidney injury model, casp1 knockout mice showed upregulated hypoxia and mitophagy pathways; no colitis outcome was measured.
Gut microbiome sequencing methods paper; ICE appears only as the word for storage on ice.

quote: Consistently, active IL-1beta-converting enzyme (ICE) subunit (p20) was expressed in samples from either CD or UC, whereas, in colonic mucosa from non-IBD controls, ICE was synthesized as precursor (p45) only.
summary: Active ICE (caspase-1) p20 was found in colonic mucosa from Crohn's disease and UC patients, but only the inactive precursor in non-IBD controls.

quote: The current understanding of the NLRC4 inflammasome is perhaps the most comprehensive illustration of the inflammasome paradigm: trigger (e.g. cytosolic flagellin), sensor (NAIP), nucleator (NLRC4), adaptor (ASC), and effector (CASP1).
summary: Review of the NLRC4 inflammasome in which CASP1 is the effector; it contains no UC-specific data on CASP1.
Plastics and human health commission report; ICE does not refer to caspase-1 here.

quote: NLRP1 and Casp1 siRNAs also abolished stress-induced Casp6 activation in neurons.
summary: Caspase-1 knockdown blocked stress-induced caspase-6 activation in human neurons and its knockout blocked LPS-induced activation in mouse brain; this is a neuronal study with no gut data.

quote: Andro also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages both in vivo and in vitro, as indicated by reduced expression of cleaved CASP1, disruption of NLRP3-PYCARD-CASP1 complex assembly, and lower IL1B secretion.
summary: The drug andrographolide reduced cleaved CASP1 and inflammasome assembly in a colitis-associated cancer model; CASP1 was a readout, not directly perturbed.

quote: Expression of NLRP3, Apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC), caspase-1 (CASP1), IL1B, and IL18 mRNA was significantly increased in atherosclerotic plaques compared to normal arteries.
summary: CASP1 mRNA was increased in human atherosclerotic plaques versus normal arteries; there is no UC data.
Faecal storage and microbiota study; the gene is not discussed.
Meditation and cold exposure endotoxemia study; ICE means ice cold water, not caspase-1.

quote: The investigation of the IL-1beta/IL-18 processing pathway showed an elevated number of cells with inflammasomes and increased levels of NLRP3 and cleaved CASP1/Caspase1 in Becn1+/- microglia.
summary: Cleaved caspase-1 was increased in Becn1+/- mouse microglia in an Alzheimer's disease context; there is no gut data.

quote: No Pro(2+) uptake in response to NG or TcdB was observed in Casp1(-/-) or Asc(-/-) BMDMs.
summary: Caspase-1 knockout macrophages showed no membrane pore formation after inflammasome activation, so caspase-1 drives pyroptotic pores; no colitis outcome was measured.

quote: Injection of these mice with low-dose LPS resulted in elevated serum TNF levels compared with Nlrp3L351P Casp1/11-/- mice and Il1b-/- Il18-/- littermates.
summary: Casp1/11 deficiency was tested in NLRP3 cryopyrinopathy mice and lowered LPS-induced TNF; the model is autoinflammatory, not colitis, so direction is unclear.

quote: Targeted inhibition of ICE may represent a novel form of therapy in IBD.
summary: IBD colonic macrophages activate ICE (caspase-1), and an ICE inhibitor reduced their release of mature IL-1 beta, supporting ICE inhibition as an IBD therapy.
Cryptosporidiosis case-control study; ICE appears only in ice cream.

quote: Disruption of the caspase 1 and caspase 11 genes in DKO mice (DKO/Casp1/11(-/-) mice) decreased the development of colitis and cancer, characterized by reduced colonic thickening, hyperplasia, inflammatory infiltrate, and tumors compared with DKO mice.
summary: Deleting caspase-1 and caspase-11 reduced spontaneous colitis and tumours in mice lacking intestinal O-glycans.

quote: Cytokines (IL-13, IL-21, TGF-beta1), chemokines (MCP-1, MIP-1beta), angiogenic factors (VEGF), growth factors (PDGF), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), acute phase proteins (SAP), caspases, and components of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (ANG II) have been identified as important regulators of fibrosis and are being investigated as potential targets of antifibrotic drugs.
summary: MCP-1 is named only in a list of fibrosis regulators in a general fibrosis review.

quote: Monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1/CCL2) is one of the key chemokines that regulate migration and infiltration of monocytes/macrophages.
summary: General review of CCL2 structure and function in monocyte recruitment, with no UC-specific data.

quote: Treatment of macrophages with n-butyrate led to the down-regulation of lipopolysaccharide-induced proinflammatory mediators, including nitric oxide, IL-6, and IL-12, but did not affect levels of TNF-α or MCP-1.
summary: Butyrate did not change MCP-1 levels in LPS-stimulated intestinal macrophages, unlike IL-6 and IL-12.

quote: SCFAs regulate several leukocyte functions including production of cytokines (TNF-α, IL-2, IL-6 and IL-10), eicosanoids and chemokines (e.g., MCP-1 and CINC-2).
summary: Review of short chain fatty acids and inflammation that mentions MCP-1 only as one chemokine they regulate.
